title: Schur's theorem on monochromatic solutions of x + y = z
statement: Let $n \ge 1$, and let $r_n = r(3,\ldots,3)$ be the $n$-colour Ramsey number for triangles. If $S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_n$ partition the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, r_n\}$ — that is, each $S_i$ is a subset of $\{1, \ldots, r_n\}$ and every integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le r_n$ lies in exactly one of the $S_i$ — then for some $i$ the part $S_i$ contains integers $x, y, z$ (not necessarily distinct) with $x + y = z$.

Let $(S_1,S_2,\ldots,S_n)$ be any partition of the set of integers $\{1,2,\ldots,r_n\}$.
Then, for some $i$, $S_i$ contains three integers $x$, $y$ and $z$ satisfying the
equation $x+y=z$.
